results.corrected_title: Meta Q3: $34.9 billion in capex pushes free cash flow negative and the stock falls about 7 percent
results.corrected_summary: Meta reported Q3 2026 revenue of $64.6 billion on 21 October, up 26 percent and above the roughly $63.3 billion consensus. Capex was $34.9 billion, compared with $19.4 billion a year earlier. That was more than operating cash flow of about $32.8 billion, so free cash flow was about minus $2.1 billion, reportedly Meta's first negative quarter since 2012. Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex guidance to $135-145 billion (from $130-145 billion), took a roughly $10 billion settlement with state attorneys general over youth safety, and proposed a new non-voting Class C share. The stock fell about 7 percent on 22 October and Meta's five-year CDS spread hit a record.
key_facts: Capex $34.9B (Q3 2025: $19.4B); operating cash flow ~$32.8B; free cash flow ~-$2.1B
~$10B settlement with state attorneys general over youth safety; new non-voting Class C stock for AI build-out, employee compensation and acquisitions
More than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up the Muse assistant
Shares fell ~7% on 22 Oct; Reuters/Markit put the 5-year CDS at a record ~114.8 bp
results.issues: The CNBC URLs returned 403 and could not be opened. Fortune does not give the $32.8B operating cash flow figure; it comes from secondary reports in search results, which are consistent with it (one says $32.79B). The CDS record is confirmed in search snippets: Reuters/Markit says 114.79 bp, while ICE data gives an intraday high of about 119.3 bp. Fortune says the shares first rose up to 5% after hours, and the ~7% drop came in regular trading on 22 Oct. Fortune also says the settlement means about $18B in payments over a decade, depending on cooperation from TikTok and YouTube. The candidate's 'first big-tech company with negative FCF' framing was not verified.

results.corrected_title: OpenAI reportedly raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, below an earlier $1.4 trillion target
results.corrected_summary: On 22 October, CNBC and Bloomberg reported that OpenAI is close to raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation, citing people familiar with the talks. That is about $150 billion below the roughly $1.4 trillion Bloomberg reported in late September. If the full amount is raised, the post-money value would be about $1.28 trillion. Coatue and UAE investors are reportedly leading the round, which is described as a bridge to an IPO; terms are unsigned and the final size is not set.
key_facts: Up to $30B at a $1.25T pre-money valuation; ~$1.28T post-money if fully raised
Earlier reported target ~$1.4T (Bloomberg, late September); FT says the target was cut by $150B
Reported leads: Coatue and UAE investors, possibly paired with a UAE compute deal
OpenAI wants signatures by the end of the following week; terms not final; OpenAI declined to comment
March 2026 round valued OpenAI at $852B post-money; confidential IPO filing in June 2026
results.issues: The Bloomberg URL returned 403. The report rests on anonymous sources (CNBC first, then Bloomberg) and is not an announced deal. Correction: the earlier $1.4T figure was a Bloomberg report from about a month before (late September), not something presented 'earlier in October' (Implicator says 'earlier in October', TechCrunch says late September). The causes the candidate gives for the lower price ('weaker revenue figures and market turmoil') were not verified.

results.corrected_title: Chip stocks have their worst day since the summer after Lam Research flags supply constraints
results.corrected_summary: On 22 October the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 6.72 percent (773.58 points) to 10,731.98, its lowest close since 29 July, and all 30 constituents fell. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6 percent. Lam Research fell about 11.8 percent, Applied Materials about 8.2 percent, AMD about 8.1 percent, Marvell and Intel about 8 percent, and Nvidia 4.4 percent. The trigger was Lam's 21 October earnings call, where executives said supply chain constraints and limited cleanroom space would keep constraining chipmakers into 2027; worries about Meta's spending and AI financing added to the selloff.
key_facts: SOX -6.72% to 10,731.98 on 22 Oct, lowest close since 29 July; all 30 constituents down
Nasdaq Composite -2.6%, its worst day since early June; S&P 500 -1.2%
Lam Research -11.8% (to $230.15), Applied Materials -8.2%, AMD -8.1%, Nvidia -4.4%
Lam CFO Doug Bettinger: guidance 'would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints'; CEO Tim Archer pointed to cleanroom and supply constraints into 2027
Meta's negative free cash flow and AI-financing worries also weighed
results.issues: Intel's close is given as 'more than 8%' or 'about 8%' by Tech Times and Arabian Post; the candidate's 7% was a morning figure from 24/7 Wall St. Nvidia's $212.21 close appears only in FX Leaders, which labels the session 'Thursday, October 23' even though 22 Oct 2026 is the Thursday, so the price is only weakly confirmed and was left out of the summary. One search result gave a Lam close of -9.78%, but two sources say about -11.8%. The 'lowest close since 29 July' detail comes from a search-result snippet; I did not open a page that states it.
